title: Rawayana Achieves First Billboard No. 1 With Manuel Turizo Collab ‘Inglés en Miami’: ‘It Represents Connection’
summary: The song rises 3-1 on the Latin Rhythm Airplay chart and marks Turizo’s seventh chart-topper.
contentText:
Venezuelan group Rawayana breaks new ground, securing its first No. 1 on a Billboard chart with the hit single “Inglés en Miami,” the group’s maiden collab with Manuel Turizo . After spending 10 weeks in the top 10, the track, part of Rawayana’s sixth studio album ¿Dónde Es El After? , rises 3-1 on the Latin Rhythm Airplay chart dated May 16.

“Having our first No. 1 on a Billboard chart means a lot to us,” Alberto “Beto” Montenegro, Rawayana’s lead vocalist tells Billboard . “We’ve spent years building our sound from Venezuela to the world, always trusting our instincts and our culture. To reach this moment with a song like ‘Inglés en Miami’ feels really special because it represents connection — different worlds, accents and energies coming together naturally.”

“Inglés en Miami” takes the lead on Latin Rhythm Airplay after a 27% gain in audience impressions across Latin rhythm radio stations in the United States, to 6.2 million, earned during the May 1-7 tracking week, according to Luminate.

The achievement marks a career milestone for Rawayana, who previously reached a No. 8 high on Latin Pop Airplay and Tropical Airplay through “La Culpa,” with Kany García, in February 2025. On Latin Rhythm Airplay, prior to “Inglés,” The group achieved a No. 20 high with “Boom Boom,” with Justin Quiles, in 2024.

“Inglés en Miami” adds a seventh No. 1 to Turizo’s growing list of hits. The Colombian last ruled the ranking with “Mamasota,” with Yandel, for two weeks in 2024. His longest leading No. 1, though, remains “Vaina Loca,” his 2018 team-up with Ozuna, which held the top spot for three consecutive weeks.

“Manuel is an incredible artist and brother, and collaborating with him on this record was effortless from day one,” Montenegro adds. “We’re grateful to everyone who made this song part of their lives.”

Rawayana achieves a notable breakthrough on the overall Latin Airplay chart as “Inglés en Miami” surges 18-4. Previously, its track “La Culpa,” with García, reached its peak at No. 47 in 2025.

For Turizo, he adds a 16th top 10 on Latin Airplay, the highest total for any artist who debuted on the chart starting in 2018.

Before topping Latin Rhythm Airplay, “Inglés” enjoyed notable success across various rankings. In April, it reached No. 26 on the Hot Latin Songs chart and No. 4 on Hot Latin Rhythm Songs. Earlier, it peaked at No. 19 on the Billboard Colombia Hot 100 in March, while climbed to No. 11 on the Peru Songs chart and No. 14 on the Ecuador Songs chart in February.
